sanskrit: avaśyaṃ ca tvayā bhūmir iyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakā bhartṛbhiḥ saha bhoktavyā nirdvaṃdveti śrutaṃ mayā
english: This earth, cleared of its thorns, shall surely be enjoyed by you together with your husbands — so have I heard it said, free of all doubt.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭravadhaṃ kṛtvā vairāṇi pratiyātya ca yudhiṣṭhirasthāṃ pṛthivīṃ draṣṭāsi drupadātmaje
english: O daughter of Drupada, having slain the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and avenged all enmities, you shall see the earth established in Yudhiṣṭhira's sovereignty.

sanskrit: yās tāḥ pravrājamānāṃ tvāṃ prāhasan darpamohitāḥ tāḥ kṣipraṃ hatasaṃkalpā drakṣyasi tvaṃ kurustriyaḥ
english: Those Kuru women who, blinded by pride, mocked you as you went into exile — you shall soon see them stripped of all their schemes and purposes.

sanskrit: tava duḥkhopapannāyā yair ācaritam apriyam viddhi saṃprasthitān sarvāṃs tān kṛṣṇe yamasādanam
english: Know, O Kṛṣṇā, that all those who have done you wrong in your affliction are already on their way to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: putras te prativindhyaś ca sutasomas tathā vibhuḥ śrutakarmārjuniś caiva śatānīkaś ca nākuliḥ sahadevāc ca yo jātaḥ śrutasenas tavātmajaḥ
english: Your sons — Prativindhya, Sutasoma, and the mighty Vibhu, Śrutakarmā the son of Arjuna, Śatānīka the son of Nakula, and Śrutasena born of Sahadeva — all your children thrive.

sanskrit: sarve kuśalino vīrāḥ kṛtāstrāś ca sutās tava abhimanyur iva prītā dvāravatyāṃ ratā bhṛśam
english: All your heroic sons are well and trained in arms; like Abhimanyu, they are joyful and deeply content in Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: tvam ivaiṣāṃ subhadrā ca prītyā sarvātmanā sthitā prīyate bhāvanirdvaṃdvā tebhyaś ca vigatajvarā
english: Subhadrā stands by them with complete devotion, just as you would; she cherishes them with wholehearted affection, her mind undivided, free of anxiety toward them.

sanskrit: bheje sarvātmanā caiva pradyumnajananī tathā bhānuprabhṛtibhiś cainān viśinaṣṭi ca keśavaḥ
english: Pradyumna's mother also serves them with entire devotion, and Keśava himself distinguishes them with the favor of Bhānu and others of his kin.

sanskrit: bhojanācchādane caiṣāṃ nityaṃ me śvaśuraḥ sthitaḥ rāmaprabhṛtayaḥ sarve bhajanty andhakavṛṣṇayaḥ tulyo hi praṇayas teṣāṃ pradyumnasya ca bhāmini
english: My father-in-law constantly attends to their food and clothing; Rāma and all the Andhaka-Vṛṣṇi heroes honor them, and their affection for the boys equals that shown to Pradyumna himself, O fair one.

sanskrit: evamādi priyaṃ prītyā hṛdyam uktvā manonugam gamanāya manaś cakre vāsudevarathaṃ prati
english: Having thus spoken these and other pleasing, heartfelt words that gladdened the mind, he turned his thoughts toward departing and toward his chariot, the chariot of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kṛṣṇamahiṣī cakārābhipradakṣiṇam āruroha rathaṃ śaureḥ satyabhāmā ca bhāminī
english: Kṛṣṇa's queen Satyabhāmā, that spirited woman, made a reverential circumambulation of Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) and then mounted the chariot of Śauri (Kṛṣṇa).

sanskrit: smayitvā tu yaduśreṣṭho draupadīṃ parisāntvya ca upāvartya tataḥ śīghrair hayaiḥ prāyāt paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then the best of the Yadus, scorcher of foes, smiled gently, consoled Draupadī once more, turned his swift horses around, and departed.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ vane vartamānā narāgryāḥ; śītoṣṇavātātapakarśitāṅgāḥ saras tad āsādya vanaṃ ca puṇyaṃ; tataḥ paraṃ kim akurvanta pārthāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: While those foremost of men lived in the forest, their bodies worn by cold, heat, wind, and sun, having reached that lake and that sacred woodland — what did the Pārthas do thereafter?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saras tad āsādya tu pāṇḍuputrā; janaṃ samutsṛjya vidhāya caiṣām vanāni ramyāṇy atha parvatāṃś ca; nadīpradeśāṃś ca tadā viceruḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having reached that lake, the sons of Pāṇḍu took leave of their attendants, made arrangements for them, and then roamed through the lovely forests, mountains, and river regions.

sanskrit: tathā vane tān vasataḥ pravīrān; svādhyāyavantaś ca tapodhanāś ca abhyāyayur vedavidaḥ purāṇās; tān pūjayām āsur atho narāgryāḥ
english: As those great warriors dwelt in the forest, ancient sages who were versed in the Vedas and rich in austerities came to them; and those foremost of men honored those sages duly.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit kuśalaḥ kathāsu; vipro 'bhyagacchad bhuvi kauraveyān sa taiḥ sametyātha yadṛcchayaiva; vaicitravīryaṃ nṛpam abhyagacchat
english: Then, on a certain occasion, a Brahmin skilled in narration came to the Kauravas (Pāṇḍavas) on earth; having met with them by chance, he went on and visited the king Vaicitravīrya (Dhṛtarāṣṭra).

sanskrit: athopaviṣṭaḥ pratisatkṛtaś ca; vṛddhena rājñā kurusattamena pracoditaḥ san kathayāṃ babhūva; dharmānilendraprabhavān yamau ca
english: Having been seated and duly honored, urged on by the aged king, that best of Kurus, he told the tale of those born of Dharma, the Wind, Indra, and the twin Aśvins.

sanskrit: kṛśāṃś ca vātātapakarśitāṅgān; duḥkhasya cograsya mukhe prapannān tāṃ cāpy anāthām iva vīranāthāṃ; kṛṣṇāṃ parikleśaguṇena yuktām
english: He described them as thin, their limbs wasted by wind and sun, plunged into the jaws of severe suffering, and Kṛṣṇā too — she who has heroes as her lords yet looked helpless as one without a protector — beset by every manner of affliction.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathāṃ tasya niśamya rājā; vaicitravīryaḥ kṛpayābhitaptaḥ vane sthitān pārthivaputrapautrāñ; śrutvā tadā duḥkhanadīṃ prapannān
english: Then, hearing that account, King Vaicitravīrya (Dhṛtarāṣṭra) was consumed with compassion; having heard that the sons and grandsons of kings were in the forest, plunged into a river of sorrow,

sanskrit: provāca dainyābhihatāntarātmā; niḥśvāsabāṣpopahataḥ sa pārthān vācaṃ kathaṃ cit sthiratām upetya; tat sarvam ātmaprabhavaṃ vicintya
english: his inner soul struck down by wretchedness, overwhelmed by sighs and tears, he somehow regained composure and, reflecting that all of this had sprung from himself, he spoke these words about the Pārthas.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu satyaḥ śucir āryavṛtto; jyeṣṭhaḥ sutānāṃ mama dharmarājaḥ ajātaśatruḥ pṛthivītalasthaḥ; śete purā rāṅkavakūṭaśāyī
english: How is it that Dharmarāja, the truthful, the pure, the noble-natured, the eldest of my sons, he who has no enemy born against him — he who once slept on a palace couch — now lies on the bare ground?

sanskrit: prabodhyate māgadhasūtapūgair; nityaṃ stuvadbhiḥ svayam indrakalpaḥ patatrisaṃghaiḥ sa jaghanyarātre; prabodhyate nūnam iḍātalasthaḥ
english: He who was ever woken by throngs of Māgadha bards with constant hymns of praise, who is himself like Indra — now he is woken in the last watch of the night surely by flocks of birds, lying on the bare earth.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu vātātapakarśitāṅgo; vṛkodaraḥ kopapariplutāṅgaḥ śete pṛthivyām atathocitāṅgaḥ; kṛṣṇāsamakṣaṃ vasudhātalasthaḥ
english: How does Vṛkodara, his limbs wasted by wind and sun, his body flooded with suppressed rage, he whose limbs deserve no such hardship, lie on the surface of the earth before the eyes of Kṛṣṇā?

sanskrit: tathārjunaḥ sukumāro manasvī; vaśe sthito dharmasutasya rājñaḥ vidūyamānair iva sarvagātrair; dhruvaṃ na śete vasatīr amarṣāt
english: And Arjuna — so tender, so high-minded — remaining under the authority of the king, Dharma's son, with all his limbs as if trembling with indignation, surely does not sleep through the night-watches from sheer impatience.

sanskrit: yamau ca kṛṣṇāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca; bhīmaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sukhaviprayuktān viniḥśvasan sarpa ivogratejā; dhruvaṃ na śete vasatīr amarṣāt
english: Seeing the twins and Kṛṣṇā, Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma all deprived of happiness, he heaves deep sighs like a fierce-glowing serpent and surely does not sleep through the night-watches from impatience.

sanskrit: tathā yamau cāpy asukhau sukhārhau; samṛddharūpāv amarau divīva prajāgarasthau dhruvam apraśāntau; dharmeṇa satyena ca vāryamāṇau
english: Likewise the twins, though worthy of every comfort, are unhappy; like immortals in heaven they are handsome and radiant, yet surely they lie awake, unable to find peace, restrained only by righteousness and truth.

sanskrit: samīraṇenāpi samo balena; samīraṇasyaiva suto balīyān sa dharmapāśena sitogratejā; dhruvaṃ viniḥśvasya sahaty amarṣam
english: Equal in strength even to the wind, and Bhīma the son of the Wind is mightier still; bound by the cord of righteousness, fierce in his blazing energy, he surely endures his wrath only with deep sighs.

sanskrit: sa cāpi bhūmau parivartamāno; vadhaṃ sutānāṃ mama kāṅkṣamāṇaḥ satyena dharmeṇa ca vāryamāṇaḥ; kālaṃ pratīkṣaty adhiko raṇe 'nyaiḥ
english: He, tossing upon the ground, craving to slay my sons, restrained only by truth and righteousness, awaits the appointed time — he who surpasses all others in battle.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrau tu jite nikṛtyā; duḥśāsano yat paruṣāṇy avocat tāni praviṣṭāni vṛkodarāṅgaṃ; dahanti marmāgnir ivendhanāni
english: The harsh words that Duḥśāsana spoke when Ajātaśatru was conquered by deceit — those words have entered Vṛkodara's body and burn in his vital parts like a fire fed by fuel.

sanskrit: na pāpakaṃ dhyāsyati dharmaputro; dhanaṃjayaś cāpy anuvartate tam araṇyavāsena vivardhate tu; bhīmasya kopo 'gnir ivānilena
english: Dharma's son will not contemplate a sinful act, and Dhanaṃjaya follows his lead; but through the forest sojourn, Bhīma's wrath grows ever greater, like a fire fed by the wind.

sanskrit: sa tena kopena vidīryamāṇaḥ; karaṃ kareṇābhinipīḍya vīraḥ viniḥśvasaty uṣṇam atīva ghoraṃ; dahann ivemān mama putrapautrān
english: That hero, torn apart by that wrath, presses one palm against the other and exhales fierce, scorching breath — as if burning these sons and grandsons of mine with it.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvadhanvā ca vṛkodaraś ca; saṃrambhiṇāv antakakālakalpau na śeṣayetāṃ yudhi śatrusenāṃ; śarān kirantāv aśaniprakāśān
english: The wielder of the Gāṇḍīva and Vṛkodara — both furious, both equal to the Ender at the time of final dissolution — showering arrows bright as thunderbolts, would leave no remnant of the enemy's army in battle.

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ śakuniḥ sūtaputro; duḥśāsanaś cāpi sumandacetāḥ madhu prapaśyanti na tu prapātaṃ; vṛkodaraṃ caiva dhanaṃjayaṃ ca
english: Duryodhana, Śakuni, the charioteer's son, and the dull-witted Duḥśāsana — they see only the honey but not the precipice; they see neither Vṛkodara nor Dhanaṃjaya for what they are.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaṃ puruṣaḥ karma kṛtvā; pratīkṣate tasya phalaṃ sma kartā sa tena yujyaty avaśaḥ phalena; mokṣaḥ kathaṃ syāt puruṣasya tasmāt
english: A man who performs an action, whether good or evil, waits as the doer for its fruit; he is joined to that fruit helplessly — how then can a man find escape from it?

sanskrit: kṣetre sukṛṣṭe hy upite ca bīje; deve ca varṣaty ṛtukālayuktam na syāt phalaṃ tasya kutaḥ prasiddhir; anyatra daivād iti cintayāmi
english: Even in a well-tilled field with seed well-sown, even when the rain-god showers in the proper season — could there be no fruit? How then could success fail to follow? Save by the decree of fate alone — so I reflect.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ matākṣeṇa yathā na sādhu; sādhupravṛttena ca pāṇḍavena mayā ca duṣputravaśānugena; yathā kurūṇām ayam antakālaḥ
english: The evil done by my sinful dice, by the righteous Pāṇḍava (Yudhiṣṭhira acting under compulsion), and by me in following the lead of my wicked son — such is the manner in which this time of destruction has come upon the Kurus.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ pravāsyaty asamīrito 'pi; dhruvaṃ prajāsyaty uta garbhiṇī yā dhruvaṃ dinādau rajanīpraṇāśas; tathā kṣapādau ca dinapraṇāśaḥ
english: Surely the wind blows even uninvited; surely a pregnant woman will bring forth her child; surely night perishes at the onset of day, and likewise day perishes at the onset of night — all is certain.

sanskrit: kriyeta kasmān na pare ca kuryur; vittaṃ na dadyuḥ puruṣāḥ kathaṃ cit prāpyārthakālaṃ ca bhaved anarthaḥ; kathaṃ nu tat syād iti tat kutaḥ syāt
english: Why then should some act while others do not? Why should men not give away wealth? Why should adversity come even after the right moment for success has been reached? How could such a thing be — and from where does it arise?

sanskrit: kathaṃ na bhidyeta na ca sraveta; na ca prasicyed iti rakṣitavyam arakṣyamāṇaḥ śatadhā viśīryed; dhruvaṃ na nāśo 'sti kṛtasya loke
english: How should something not crack, not leak, not spill? — thus it must be guarded; left unguarded it would shatter into a hundred pieces. Surely what has been done does not perish from the world.

sanskrit: gato hy araṇyād api śakralokaṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ paśyata vīryam asya astrāṇi divyāni caturvidhāni; jñātvā punar lokam imaṃ prapannaḥ
english: For Dhanaṃjaya has gone even from the forest to the world of Śakra — behold his valor! He has mastered the fourfold divine weapons and returned to this world once more.

sanskrit: svargaṃ hi gatvā saśarīra eva; ko mānuṣaḥ punar āgantum icchet anyatra kālopahatān anekān; samīkṣamāṇas tu kurūn mumūrṣūn
english: For what mortal man, having gone bodily to heaven, would wish to return — save one who, looking upon the many Kurus struck down by time and hastening to their doom, cannot stay away?

sanskrit: dhanurgrāhaś cārjunaḥ savyasācī; dhanuś ca tad gāṇḍivaṃ lokasāram astrāṇi divyāni ca tāni tasya; trayasya tejaḥ prasaheta ko nu
english: And Arjuna the ambidextrous archer, and that bow the Gāṇḍīva which is the essence of the world, and his divine weapons — who could withstand the combined blazing energy of those three?

sanskrit: niśamya tad vacanaṃ pārthivasya; duryodhano rahite saubalaś ca abodhayat karṇam upetya sarvaṃ; sa cāpy ahṛṣṭo 'bhavad alpacetāḥ
english: Hearing those words of the king, Duryodhana and Śakuni (Saubala) went to a private place and informed Karṇa of everything; and he too became displeased — that one of small understanding.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya tad vākyaṃ niśamya sahasaubalaḥ duryodhanam idaṃ kāle karṇo vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Karṇa, along with Śakuni (Saubala), spoke these words at the right moment to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: pravrājya pāṇḍavān vīrān svena vīryeṇa bhārata bhuṅkṣvemāṃ pṛthivīm eko divaṃ śambarahā yathā
english: O Bhārata, having banished the heroic Pāṇḍavas by your own valor, enjoy this earth alone, as the slayer of Śambara (Indra) enjoys heaven.

sanskrit: prācyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca pratīcyodīcyavāsinaḥ kṛtāḥ karapradāḥ sarve rājānas te narādhipa
english: The kings of the East, the South, the West, and the North — all have been made tribute-payers to you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yā hi sā dīpyamāneva pāṇḍavān bhajate purā sādya lakṣmīs tvayā rājann avāptā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: That Lakṣmī which once shone resplendently and cleaved to the Pāṇḍavas — that very Lakṣmī has now been won by you, O king, along with your brothers.

sanskrit: indraprasthagate yāṃ tāṃ dīpyamānāṃ yudhiṣṭhire apaśyāma śriyaṃ rājann aciraṃ śokakarśitāḥ
english: That blazing Śrī which we witnessed residing in Yudhiṣṭhira at Indraprastha — O king, we who were lately wasted by grief now see her here with us.

sanskrit: sā tu buddhibaleneyaṃ rājñas tasmād yudhiṣṭhirāt tvayākṣiptā mahābāho dīpyamāneva dṛśyate
english: That very Śrī has been wrested by you, O mighty-armed one, from King Yudhiṣṭhira by the power of your intellect, and she is seen shining brilliantly here.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava rājendra rājānaḥ paravīrahan śāsane 'dhiṣṭhitāḥ sarve kiṃ kurma iti vādinaḥ
english: Likewise, O lord of kings, slayer of enemy heroes, all the kings are established under your command, saying, 'What are your orders?'

sanskrit: tavādya pṛthivī rājan nikhilā sāgarāmbarā saparvatavanā devī sagrāmanagarākarā nānāvanoddeśavatī pattanair upaśobhitā
english: Today, O king, the entire earth is yours — she who is ocean-girt, adorned with mountains and forests, the divine one filled with villages, cities, and mines, replete with every kind of woodland tract and beautified with port towns.

sanskrit: vandyamāno dvijai rājan pūjyamānaś ca rājabhiḥ pauruṣād divi deveṣu bhrājase raśmivān iva
english: Worshipped by Brahmins, O king, and honored by kings, through your own prowess you blaze among the gods in heaven like the sun with his rays.

sanskrit: rudrair iva yamo rājā marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ kurubhis tvaṃ vṛto rājan bhāsi nakṣatrarāḍ iva
english: As Yama is surrounded by the Rudras, and Vāsava by the Maruts, so you, O king, surrounded by the Kurus, shine like the lord of the constellations (the moon).

sanskrit: ye sma te nādriyante ''jñā nodvijante kadā ca na paśyāmas tāñ śriyā hīnān pāṇḍavān vanavāsinaḥ
english: Those who never respected your commands, who were never afraid of you — we see those very ones now: the Pāṇḍavas, stripped of prosperity, dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: śrūyante hi mahārāja saro dvaitavanaṃ prati vasantaḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sārdhaṃ brāhmaṇair vanavāsibhiḥ
english: For it is heard, O great king, that the Pāṇḍavas are dwelling near the lake in the Dvaitavana forest, together with Brahmins and forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: sa prayāhi mahārāja śriyā paramayā yutaḥ pratapan pāṇḍuputrāṃs tvaṃ raśmivān iva tejasā
english: Therefore go, O great king, endowed with supreme prosperity, scorching the sons of Pāṇḍu with your splendor as the sun with his rays.

sanskrit: sthito rājye cyutān rājyāc chriyā hīnāñ śriyā vṛtaḥ asamṛddhān samṛddhārthaḥ paśya pāṇḍusutān nṛpa
english: Established in your kingdom, yourself clothed in glory, look upon the sons of Pāṇḍu who have been cast out of the kingdom, stripped of prosperity, in want — while you have attained every wealth, O king.

sanskrit: mahābhijanasaṃpannaṃ bhadre mahati saṃsthitam pāṇḍavās tvābhivīkṣantāṃ yayātim iva nāhuṣam
english: Let the Pāṇḍavas behold you, O one endowed with great lineage, established in great station — even as they beheld Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, in his glory.

sanskrit: yāṃ śriyaṃ suhṛdaś caiva durhṛdaś ca viśāṃ pate paśyanti puruṣe dīptāṃ sā samarthā bhavaty uta
english: That prosperity which friends and foes alike behold blazing in a man — that, O lord of the people, becomes a true and effective prosperity.

sanskrit: samastho viṣamasthān hi durhṛdo yo 'bhivīkṣate jagatīsthān ivādristhaḥ kiṃ tataḥ paramaṃ sukham
english: He who, standing in ease, looks down upon enemies in misfortune — as one standing on a mountain looks down upon those on the earth — what pleasure is greater than that?

sanskrit: na putradhanalābhena na rājyenāpi vindati prītiṃ nṛpatiśārdūla yām amitrāghadarśanāt
english: Not through the gain of sons, nor wealth, nor even a kingdom does a man find the delight, O tiger among kings, that he finds from seeing the downfall of his enemies.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tasya sukhaṃ na syād āśrame yo dhanaṃjayam abhivīkṣeta siddhārtho valkalājinavāsasam
english: And what joy would there not be for one who, his own aims accomplished, sees Dhanaṃjaya in the hermitage clad in bark and deerskin?

sanskrit: suvāsaso hi te bhāryā valkalājinavāsasam paśyantv asukhitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ sā ca nirvidyatāṃ punaḥ vinindatāṃ tathātmānaṃ jīvitaṃ ca dhanacyutā
english: Your richly-dressed wives should look upon the unhappy Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) in her bark and deerskin garments; and she, bereft of wealth, should feel disgust anew and condemn both herself and her very life.

sanskrit: na tathā hi sabhāmadhye tasyā bhavitum arhati vaimanasyaṃ yathā dṛṣṭvā tava bhāryāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: For that wretchedness which befits her is not what she felt in the midst of the assembly-hall — it is what she will feel upon seeing your richly adorned wives.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu rājānaṃ karṇaḥ śakuninā saha tūṣṇīṃ babhūvatur ubhau vākyānte janamejaya
english: Having thus spoken to the king, Karṇa and Śakuni both fell silent, O Janamejaya, when their speech was done.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca karṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā duryodhanas tadā hṛṣṭo bhūtvā punar dīna idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Karṇa, King Duryodhana was at first gladdened, but then, despondent again, spoke these words.

sanskrit: bravīṣi yad idaṃ karṇa sarvaṃ me manasi sthitam na tv abhyanujñāṃ lapsyāmi gamane yatra pāṇḍavāḥ
english: What you say, Karṇa, is all that lies in my heart as well; but I shall not obtain permission to go where the Pāṇḍavas are.

sanskrit: paridevati tān vīrān dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ manyate 'bhyadhikāṃś cāpi tapoyogena pāṇḍavān
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, laments those heroes and even now considers the Pāṇḍavas superior — grown greater through the discipline of austerity.

sanskrit: atha vāpy anubudhyeta nṛpo 'smākaṃ cikīrṣitam evam apy āyatiṃ rakṣan nābhyanujñātum arhati
english: And if the king were to discover our intention — even thinking of the future — he would not grant permission.

sanskrit: na hi dvaitavane kiṃ cid vidyate 'nyat prayojanam utsādanam ṛte teṣāṃ vanasthānāṃ mama dviṣām
english: For there is no other purpose in Dvaitavana than to taunt and torment those forest-dwelling enemies of mine.

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā kṣattā dyūtakāla upasthite abravīd yac ca māṃ tvāṃ ca saubalaṃ ca vacas tadā
english: For you know how Kṣattā (Vidura) spoke at the time of the dice-game, and what he said then to me, to you, and to Śakuni (Saubala).

sanskrit: tāni pūrvāṇi vākyāni yac cānyat paridevitam vicintya nādhigacchāmi gamanāyetarāya vā
english: Reflecting on those former words and on all the lamentation since, I cannot determine whether to go or not to go.

sanskrit: mamāpi hi mahān harṣo yad ahaṃ bhīmaphalgunau kliṣṭāv araṇye paśyeyaṃ kṛṣṇayā sahitāv iti
english: Yet my own joy would be immense if I could see Bhīma and Phalguna (Arjuna) afflicted in the forest, together with Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: na tathā prāpnuyāṃ prītim avāpya vasudhām api dṛṣṭvā yathā pāṇḍusutān valkalājinavāsasaḥ
english: Even if I were to gain the whole earth, I would not obtain such delight as I would from seeing the sons of Pāṇḍu in their garments of bark and deerskin.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu syād adhikaṃ tasmād yad ahaṃ drupadātmajām draupadīṃ karṇa paśyeyaṃ kāṣāyavasanāṃ vane
english: And what could be greater than that, O Karṇa, than that I should see Draupadī, the daughter of Drupada, clad in ochre robes in the forest?

sanskrit: yadi māṃ dharmarājaś ca bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ yuktaṃ paramayā lakṣmyā paśyetāṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet
english: If Dharmarāja and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava were to see me invested with supreme prosperity — my life would be worth living.

sanskrit: upāyaṃ na tu paśyāmi yena gacchema tad vanam yathā cābhyanujānīyād gacchantaṃ māṃ mahīpatiḥ
english: Yet I see no means by which we might go to that forest in such a way that the lord of the earth would give his leave as I departed.

sanskrit: sa saubalena sahitas tathā duḥśāsanena ca upāyaṃ paśya nipuṇaṃ yena gacchema tad vanam
english: Together with Śakuni (Saubala) and likewise with Duḥśāsana, find a clever means by which we may go to that forest.

sanskrit: aham apy adya niścitya gamanāyetarāya vā kālyam eva gamiṣyāmi samīpaṃ pārthivasya ha
english: And I myself, having resolved the matter — whether to go or not — shall go to the king's presence tomorrow morning.

sanskrit: mayi tatropaviṣṭe tu bhīṣme ca kurusattame upāyo yo bhaved dṛṣṭas taṃ brūyāḥ sahasaubalaḥ
english: When I am seated there together with Bhīṣma, that best of Kurus, whatever means you see to be fit — that you should declare, along with Saubala.
